messages.subject: Range Wide Activity Map
parts:
Hi All,

I frequently see papers using NicheMapR to calculate range or continent wide conditions (like potential activity hours) for a species in a similar way as you have done in the Heteronotia binoei paper from 2004, with resulting raster outputs across the range of a species. Despite how common this seems in the literature, I have yet to come upon a standardized methodology of applying a parameterized ectotherm model across a range to produce a raster image like this, only running it at individual points. While in theory I feel like I could come up with ways to do this, I wanted to double check that there wasn’t already some built in functionality or documentation on doing this that I may be missing that you could point me in the direction of.

Thanks in advance,

Connor Hughes

messages.author: 6cec8ea3702ece93
messages.subject: Re: Range Wide Activity Map
parts:
Hi Connor,

There isn't any built-in functionality but you can do it by running through a list of points in a grid and then rasterising at the end. Here's an example:

library(NicheMapR)
library(raster)

# create a vector of latitudes and longitudes
sites <- expand.grid(seq(126, 127, 0.11), seq(-30, -29, 0.11))
colnames(sites) <- c('long', 'lat') # name columns
sites$soiltemp <- NA # add a blank column to put a variable

# loop through the sites and run the microclimate model, saving the soil temperature at 11 am
for(i in 1:nrow(sites)){
 micro <- micro_global(loc = c(sites[i, 1], sites[i, 2]), runshade = 0)
 sites$soiltemp[i] <- micro$soil[12, 3]
}

# create a grid
lat1<-min(sites[, 2]) - 0.065 # min latitude
lat2<-max(sites[, 2]) + 0.065 # max latitude
lon1<-min(sites[, 1]) - 0.065 # min longitude
lon2<-max(sites[, 1]) + 0.065 # max longitude
quadwid <- (lon2 - lon1) / 0.11
quadlen <- (lat2 - lat1) / 0.11
gridout <- raster(ncol = quadwid, nrow = quadlen, xmn = lon1, xmx = lon2, ymn = lat1, ymx = lat2)

# put the results in the grid
x <- cbind(sites$long, sites$lat) # list of co-ordinates
grid <- rasterize(x, gridout, sites[, 3])
grid <- projectRaster(grid, crs="+proj=longlat +datum=WGS84") # change projection here if needed

plot(grid)

All the best,
Mike
